thread:
maria (AE): Heads-up — customer 'Northfield Bank' wants a week-long POC in an isolated DC. They require fully offline delivery, signed artifacts, and explicit upgrade windows. Can we support a locked bundle + delta patch flow?
sam (SE): Short answer: yes, but there are a few constraints. We can ship an immutable bundle + signed delta updates. Need to confirm bundle size, offline transfer method, and their allowed maintenance windows.
maria (AE): Bundle size limit? They mentioned air-gapped import via SFTP over an ops jumpbox — might prefer small chunks.
sam (SE): We typically recommend minibundles (<4GB) for islanded sites to avoid long transfer times. For larger models we'll split runtime vs model shards.
neil (eng-infra): Also flag: KV cache warm-up on first boot will spike disk IO; if they only allow night windows, plan for a staged rollout — node-by-node.
sara (CS): Their support SLA requires a 48-hr turnaround for critical patches during the POC. We need to confirm we can meet that for signed deltas.
phil (security): Security questionnaire items to flag: 1) SBOM availability for each bundle 2) bundle signing algorithm (we use RSA-4096 + timestamping) 3) offline KMS integration — do they have an HSM? 4) audit logging retention in private deploy.
maria (AE): They do have an on-prem HSM (Thales). They want to know if Redwood can integrate for at-rest key wrapping.
sam (SE): Yes — we support customer-managed KMS via PKCS#11 in Private mode. For airgap we'll provide a key-encryption-key workflow: bundle encrypted with CEK, CEK wrapped by customer KMS. We need their KMS admin to provide a cert and allowed endpoints (or local socket).
phil (security): Need to include this in the security response: we never persist unwrapped CEKs and require mutual TLS for control-plane syncs. For offline installs we can accept signed manifests and signed bundle checksums.
maria (AE): Pricing question from procurement: What's the licensing/upgrade cadence cost if they want quarterly security patches vs monthly?
sam (SE): Pricing can be structured: base Private license + optional security cadence tiers. Quarterly patches are included in standard enterprise; monthly accelerated patching is a premium. I'll loop in sales ops with numbers.
neil (eng-infra): Ops note: If they insist on no outbound connectivity ever, we can't rely on automatic telemetry or license checks. We'll provide an offline activation token (time-limited) and a manual usage report tooling. That affects diagnostics.
sara (CS): Make sure runbook includes how to collect core dumps and logs for us — they must zip to the jumpbox and we’ll consume.
maria (AE): They're also asking about rollback window in case a delta patch fails — they want automatic rollback to previous bundle. Is that supported?
sam (SE): We support atomic upgrades with one-step rollback to previous image if the node fails health checks within the grace period. Rollback must be triggered within the maintenance window otherwise ops will require manual intervention.
phil (security): Add to Q: Do we provide reproducible build info for the runtime and model quantization? They asked for supply-chain provenance.
neil (eng-infra): We can provide SBOM + git commit hashes + build container digest. For model weights we provide model provenance metadata (source model, quantization script hash).
maria (AE): Ok — next steps: sam to draft a short technical attachment for SOW listing: bundle sizes, patch cadence options, KMS/HSM steps, offline activation flow, rollback behavior, and required maintenance windows. Phil to add security answers. Sara to include support SLA addendum. I'll send to customer by EOD tomorrow.
sam (SE): On it. I'll post a draft here when ready.
phil (security): I'll prepare a one-page security bullet list and the SBOM export sample.
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline queued for bundle-signing-job #4589 — status: waiting on manual key-confirmation.
maria (AE): Thanks everyone. If you can drop estimated timelines for the SOW pieces here that helps procurement. :pray:
